# Clarence Gets a Bargain

> A 36-page children's financial literacy picture book (ages 6-10, grades 1-5) written and illustrated by Jonathan Bach. A boy earns a robot reward and completes one real purchase from start to finish — reading sale ads ("shopping homework"), comparison shopping, finding a clearance markdown, redeeming a 10%-off coupon at the register, and paying sales tax. Kids open it as impulsive little spenders and close it as aware, educated consumers. Built as a read-along for a kid and a grown-up — a money-talk starter by design. 16+ financial concepts taught through the story, never as a worksheet. Includes a 21-term financial glossary with page references.

Key facts: ISBN 979-8-234-07638-0; LCCN 2026906164; hardbound, full color, 11x8.5", 36 pages; $19.99 direct from the publisher; Est. Lexile AD 620L. Aligned to five standards frameworks: Jump$tart National Standards, Common Core Math, Common Core ELA, Council for Economic Education (CEE), and FDIC Money Smart for Young People. Endorsed by Maryann Milewski Moskal (veteran K-5 educator, 30+ years) and Wally Luckeydoo, Ed.D. (2026 EIFLE Educator of the Year; 2026 Jump$tart Corey Carlisle Award).

What makes it different: most children's money books cover earning or saving (piggy banks, lemonade stands). This is the one that teaches spending — the complete consumer transaction, including the point of sale. Core concept: Wants vs. Needs.

## Author and social

Jonathan Bach is the author and illustrator. He is a real estate finance and title attorney and mixed-media artist. He is not David Bach, the adult personal-finance author, and not Jonathan Bach the author of "Above the Clouds."
